** How the information was gathered
<<part0-method>>

The information in this document was gathered from the following sources, in decreasing order of reliability:

1. Analysis of the source code
2. Observation of the production and test environments
3. Interviews with the technical contacts (see [[file:references.org::references-interviews][References -- Interviews]])
4. Existing documentation (see [[file:references.org::references-documents][References -- Documents]])

Every statement not verified in the code is marked =[TO VALIDATE]=.  The discrepancies found between actual and expected behavior are marked =[FINDING]=.

** How to read this document
<<part0-reading>>

The document has six parts, for different readers:

| Part | Content                    | Read it if you are...         |
|------+----------------------------+-------------------------------|
| 0    | Preliminaries and glossary | Everyone                      |
| I    | Enterprise view            | Executives, senior architects |
| II   | Architecture by component  | Architects, developers        |
| III  | Functional specifications  | Analysts, product owners, BU  |
| IV   | Infrastructure census      | IT operations, sysadmins      |
| V    | NFR and constraints        | Architects, IT management     |

Marking conventions used in the document:
- =[TO VALIDATE]= -- statement not verified with the customer
- =[TO REVIEW]= -- produced by an automatic process, not reviewed
- =[FINDING]= -- discrepancy between actual and expected behavior
- =[APPROVED YYYY-MM-DD]= -- section validated by the customer on that date
- =[SOURCE: X]= -- specific origin of the information

Graphical notations:
- C4 diagrams (L1-L3): static structure of the systems
- UML sequence diagrams: interaction flows at run time
- UML activity diagrams with swimlanes: business processes
- DFD: data flows and integrations
- UML deployment diagrams: infrastructure topology
